content.text: When an object's velocity changes, we say it is accelerating. Acceleration is one of the most important concepts in physics, linking forces to changes in motion. Understanding acceleration is key to analysing everything from car journeys to rocket launches.

Acceleration is NOT the same as speed or velocity. Acceleration tells you how quickly the velocity is changing. An object can be moving fast with zero acceleration (constant velocity), or moving slowly with large acceleration (rapidly speeding up).

An object has zero acceleration when:
It is moving at constant velocity (including constant direction)
An acceleration of 2 m/s² means the velocity increases by 2 m/s every second.

The formula a = (v - u) / t uses v for final velocity, u for initial velocity, and t for time. A positive result means speeding up (in the positive direction); a negative result means deceleration or acceleration in the opposite direction.

## Acceleration Due to Gravity

Near Earth's surface, all objects in free fall experience the same acceleration:

$$g \approx 9.8 \text{ m/s}^2 \approx 10 \text{ m/s}^2
Independent of mass (in the absence of air resistance)
Varies slightly with location and altitude
Car specifications often quote 0-60 mph times, which relate to acceleration
Racing cars have very high accelerations
Sprinters have high acceleration at the start of a race
A golf ball experiences huge acceleration during impact with the club
Rockets need sustained acceleration to reach orbital velocity
Astronauts experience high g-forces during launch and re-entry
Airbags and crumple zones increase the time of deceleration in crashes, reducing forces on passengers

Deceleration does not mean negative acceleration in all cases. Deceleration means the object is slowing down. If an object moves in the negative direction and decelerates, its acceleration is actually positive. Always think about whether the object is speeding up or slowing down.
— Acceleration means any change in velocity, including slowing down and changing direction.
— Deceleration is slowing down. This could be negative acceleration (if moving in the positive direction) or positive acceleration (if moving in the negative direction).
— Not necessarily! A ball thrown upward has zero velocity at its highest point but is still accelerating downward due to gravity.
— No! Constant acceleration means velocity is changing at a constant rate.
— Without air resistance, all objects fall with the same acceleration (demonstrated by Galileo).
